questions.question: South Africa's three great topographic units are:
options: The interior plateau, the Great Escarpment and the marginal or coastal zone
The Highveld, the Lowveld and the Bushveld only
Three mountain ranges along the coast
The Kalahari, the Karoo and the Cape Flats

questions.question: The interior plateau mostly stands at:
options: Sea level
Between about 1 200 and 1 800 metres above sea level
Above 4 000 metres
Below 300 metres

questions.question: The Great Escarpment reaches its highest, sharpest section in:
options: The Cape Flats
The Kalahari
The KwaZulu-Natal DRAKENSBERG, rising above 3 000 metres
The West Coast

questions.question: A convex slope is one that:
options: Holds a single constant angle like a plank
Hollows inward like a saucer
Is perfectly vertical
Bulges outward, STEEPENING downhill like the shoulder of a dome

questions.question: The four slope elements in order from the top down are:
options: Crest, cliff, talus slope, pediment
Pediment, talus, cliff, crest
Cliff, crest, pediment, talus
Crest, pediment, cliff, talus

questions.question: The cliff is called the free face because:
options: It is free of any rock
Rock freed from it by weathering FALLS AWAY immediately instead of lying where it was loosened
Anyone may climb it without paying
It faces away from the wind

questions.question: The talus or debris slope is straight because:
options: It is cut from solid rock
Bulldozers grade it
Loose rock settles at its ANGLE OF REPOSE, generally between about 25 and 35 degrees
Water polishes it flat

questions.question: The pediment is:
options: The steepest element of the profile
A pile of loose boulders
The convex hilltop
A gently CONCAVE bedrock surface, usually under about 5 degrees, sweeping from the slope foot to the plain

subtopics.title: Slope Retreat — How the Profile Moves

questions.question: In parallel slope retreat, the profile:
options: Keeps its proportions — cliff steep, talus at repose, pediment gentle — while relocating BACKWARD, widening the pediment
Flattens and rounds until the cliff disappears
Grows steeper every year
Stays exactly where it is

questions.question: When opposing slopes retreat away from each other over deep time:
options: The upland grows larger
Pediments from neighbouring valleys meet and merge into a PEDIPLAIN, leaving koppies and inselbergs as survivors
A canyon always forms
The talus buries the whole landscape

questions.question: South African conditions favour parallel retreat over slope decline because:
options: The country has no slopes
Heavy year-round rain rounds everything
Semi-arid climates, resistant caprocks and sparse vegetation keep cliffs sharp while soft material is stripped
Earthquakes constantly renew the cliffs

questions.question: Human activity is best placed on the slope profile as:
options: Houses on the cliff and crops on the talus
Roads straight up the free face
Everything at the foot of an active talus
Settlement, ploughing and roads on gentle crests and pediments — with rockfall and erosion risk on the cliff and talus zones

subtopics.title: GIS — Resolution, Data Types, Raster and Vector

questions.question: Spatial resolution is:
options: The size of the ground area represented by ONE PIXEL — finer resolution shows smaller detail
The number of wavelength bands a sensor records
The speed of the satellite
The number of colours on a printed map

questions.question: High spectral resolution matters because:
options: It makes the image larger
More, narrower wavelength bands let analysts tell apart healthy veld, stressed crops, bare soil and water by their different reflections
It shows individual people
It removes clouds from images

questions.question: In vector data, a borehole, a river and a farm are stored respectively as:
options: Area, point, line
Line, area, point
POINT, LINE and AREA — each with attribute data attached
Three raster grids

questions.question: Raster data suits phenomena like altitude and rainfall because:
options: They have sharp edges
They never change
They only occur at points
They vary CONTINUOUSLY across the land, which a grid of valued cells captures naturally

subtopics.title: The Country Is a Three-Step Staircase

questions.question: In the book-on-the-table model, the book's edges stand for:
options: The GREAT ESCARPMENT — the sudden drop from plateau toward the coast
The coastal beaches
The Kalahari dunes
The rivers of the Highveld

questions.question: The Tugela river illustrates the staircase by:
options: Flowing uphill onto the plateau
Plunging nearly 950 metres off the Drakensberg rim in one of the world's tallest waterfalls
Disappearing underground
Flowing along the top of the escarpment forever

questions.question: The shoulder, the soup spoon and the plank teach the slope shapes:
options: Compound, vertical and rolling
Steep, gentle and flat
CONVEX — steepening over the roll; CONCAVE — flattening to the bottom; RECTILINEAR — one constant angle
North-facing, south-facing and east-facing

questions.question: In the production-line picture, the cliff is the factory because:
options: It is where solid rock is broken off and dropped to the slope below
It manufactures soil from rain
Workers quarry it daily
It is the flattest part of the hill

questions.question: A pile of builder's sand always settles at the same slope because:
options: Builders shape it deliberately
Loose material can rest no steeper than its ANGLE OF REPOSE — extra material slides until the resting angle returns
Sand is sticky
Gravity is weaker on small piles

questions.question: The chant for the four elements runs:
options: Crest concave, cliff gentle, talus curved, pediment vertical
Crest straight, cliff straight, talus straight, pediment straight
Crest convex, cliff vertical, talus straight, pediment concave
Crest vertical, cliff convex, talus concave, pediment straight

questions.question: A hill in soft-rock country with no resistant band will lack:
options: A crest
A pediment
All four elements
The CLIFF and its talus — leaving a smooth profile of scalp and apron

subtopics.title: The Hill That Walks and the Map Made of Lego

questions.question: The 'walking hill' image captures the fact that:
options: The whole profile shifts BACKWARD with its proportions intact — cliff sheer, chute at its angle, apron gentle — as retreat proceeds
Hills physically slide across the plain
The profile softens into a dome as it ages
The pediment moves up the hill

questions.question: Run parallel retreat for tens of millions of years and the result is:
options: A deeper canyon
Merged aprons forming a PEDIPLAIN with surviving koppies standing on it — the Karoo picture
A higher plateau
A row of volcanoes

questions.question: In the Lego-against-graph-paper picture:
options: Lego is raster and graph paper is vector
Both are raster
VECTOR is the Lego — crisp points, lines and areas with attribute tables; RASTER is the graph paper — a grid of valued cells
Neither stores map data

questions.question: Feeding a raster elevation model into a GIS lets an analyst:
options: Change the height of the mountains
Predict earthquakes
Make rain fall on the pediment
Calculate the steepness of every hillside in a province in seconds — the map a soil conservation officer or road engineer needs
